## Research interests

My research interests lie at the intersection of Bayesian statistics,
Bayesian nonparametrics, statistical network analysis, and computational
statistics.

I am particularly interested in developing flexible Bayesian models for
complex and structured data, with a focus on network data and scalable
computational methods.

## Current research

### Bayesian modeling of network data

My research focuses on Bayesian nonparametric methods for modeling
heterogeneous populations of networks. The goal is to develop flexible
models that can capture both common structural features and
heterogeneity across networks.

In this context, I develop Bayesian models based on nonparametric
mixture constructions, together with computational methods for
posterior inference and applications to real network data.

### Longitudinal brain network analysis

I am also working on Bayesian methods for the analysis of longitudinal
brain networks, with applications to neurodegenerative diseases.

The research aims to model changes in brain network topology over time
while accounting for heterogeneity across individuals and avoiding the
need to fix the number of network communities in advance.

## Publications

### Bayesian Nonparametric Modeling of Heterogeneous Populations of Networks

**Francesco Barile, Luis E. Lunagómez, Bernardo Nipoti**

*Bayesian Analysis*, 2026.

This work develops a Bayesian nonparametric framework for modeling
heterogeneous populations of networks. The model provides a flexible
representation of network populations while allowing for the
identification of representative network structures and patterns of
heterogeneity.

[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1214/26-BA1588)

### Control Variate-based Stochastic Sampling from the Probability Simplex

**Francesco Barile, coauthor**

*Statistics and Computing*.

This work develops a variance-reduced stochastic sampling method for
probability-simplex distributions, with applications to Bayesian
models such as latent Dirichlet allocation and mixed-membership
stochastic block models.

[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00845)

## Software

I develop computational tools in R and C++ for Bayesian inference and

My research software and reproducible code are available on
